entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have heard learned counsel for both sides.

By the present petition under Article 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner, who is owner of land, prays for declaration of lapsing of reservation in view of section 127 of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 ( 'the MRTP Act'), in respect of Site Nos.14 and 15, out of Gat No 239 (Survey No. 379), situated at Majalgaon, Dist.Beed.
3.

entities.text: Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is stated that the development plan for the Municipal Council, Majalgaon was sanctioned by the Government of Maharashtra vide Notification published on 02.09.2000.

In the said plan, the lands of the petitioner i.e. Site No.14 admeasuring 23R and Site No. 15 admeasuring 40 R out of Gat No.
239 (Old Survey No. 379) situated at Majalgaon were reserved for shopping Centre/Vegitable Market and Primary School/Playground, respectively.
However, no steps have been initiated by Respondent/ planning authority for acquisition of the said property for more than 20 years.
Therefore, the petitioner issued purchase notice dated 20.04.2016 under section 127 along-with necessary documents.
The notice was duly served upon respondent No.4-Chief Officer.

Thereafter,
vide letter dated 01.04.2022 addressed to the Assistant Director, Town Planning, Beed, the Chief Officer of Municipal Council, Majalgaon communicated his opinion that it would be appropriate to de-reserve Site Nos. 14 and 15 as per Section 127(2) of the Act.

However, no effective steps have been taken by the wp14223-23Beed respondents either for de-reservation or for acquisition as contemplated under section 126 of the MRTP Act read with section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 or Section 19 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, for more than two years.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, as per provisions of Section 127 of the MRTP Act, the reservation would lapse on expiry of notice period.
4. The respondents have not disputed the facts narrated by the petitioner.
The respondent No. 4 has stated about publication of notice about modification/chances in the development plan.

However,
reservation over the lands of the petitioner is not denied.

Further, it is submitted that relevant documents showing title or interest in the said land such as, property card, development plan map,
measurement map etc. were not accompanied with the notice under section 127 of the MRTP Act and, therefore, the notice is not valid.
5. The petitioner enclosed document such as 7/12 extract, having mutation entry in the revenue record in the name of the petitioner.
The respondent-Municipal council has not disputed the reservation over the land of the petitioner.
The land under reservation being owned by the petitioner and revenue record to that effect is on record, there can be no dispute over the ownership of the property.

So far as the objection as regards non production of the documents, such as measurement map and development plan map with the notice, looking to the nature of these documents, they can be said to be within knowledge and can very well be available with the respondents authority.

sentences.text: Therefore, the respondents cannot refuse to act upon the notice for want of formal documents which are already with the planning authority.

Failure on the part of the respondents in acquiring the reserved lands for the period of more than 10 years from date of notification, so also, for the period of more than two years from the date of service of notice under section 127 of the MRTP Act is not supported by any cogent and substantial reason.
Therefore, we do not see any defect in the notice issued by the petitioner.

7. In our view, the law laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Girnar Traders vs. State of Maharashtra, (2007) 7 SCC 555 and Girnar Traders vs. State of Maharashtra and others, (2011) 3 SCC 1, squarely applies to the present case.

entities.text: Girnar Traders vs. State of Maharashtra, (2007) 7 SCC 555
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Girnar Traders vs. State of Maharashtra and others, (2011) 3 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No steps, as are expected in view of the law laid down in Girnar Traders (supra), have been initiated by the Planning Authority.
As such we are inclined to allow the writ petition and declare that the reservation on land of the petitioner stands lapsed 8.
In view of the above, the Writ Petition is allowed.

The Respondent- Municipal Council/Planning Authority shall issue a letter to Respondent No.1 State, within 30 days from today, indicating that the reservation on the land of the petitioner i.e. Site No.14 admeasuring 23R and Site No. 15 admeasuring 40 R out of Gat No. 239 (Old Survey No. 379)
situated at Majalgaon reserved for shopping Centre/Vegitable Market and Primary School/Playground respectively, has lapsed.
Respondent No.1 State shall thereafter, issue a notification under Section 127(2) of the MRTP Act, within 60 days.
( Y. G. KHOBRAGADE, J. ) ( MANISH PITALE, J. )
